title: Destruction of the Kakhovka Dam floods the lower Dnipro and triggers a humanitarian emergency
body:
The Kakhovka Dam on the Dnipro River in Kherson Oblast was breached on 6 June 2023, flooding towns downstream. Ukrainian authorities reported that 40 settlements were fully or partly flooded, a figure expected to rise. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the event a monumental humanitarian, economic and environmental catastrophe and said that at least 16,000 people had lost their homes. Ukraine and Russia blamed each other. The dam is under Russian control, although Ukrainian forces hold the opposite bank, and Guterres said the UN could not independently verify how it happened.

The reservoir water cools the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant. The International Atomic Energy Agency reported a significant drop in the reservoir level but said there was no immediate risk, since the cooling supply should last a few days and a large cooling pond nearby could serve as an alternative.

The UN began sending drinking water, purification tablets and sanitation supplies. The UN human rights office warned of risks to housing, health, livelihoods and clean water, and said farming and fisheries across the region, including Russian-occupied Crimea, would be affected. UN News reported that fast-moving water might spread landmines into areas previously considered safe. General Assembly President Csaba Korosi said intentional attacks causing long-term environmental damage are war crimes, and the UN human rights office called for a full investigation and accountability.
